Regional market comparison

Questions driving the research

Business first
01 Which regions face the greatest negative price exposure?
02 When do prices fall below zero, and for how long?
03 Do regional prices move together?
04 Where could flexible storage have economic value?
Initial finding
South Australia records the most frequent negative prices. But negative price frequency is only one part of the story. The analysis also examines timing, volatility, extreme prices and trading spreads.

Negative prices over time

January to October each year

What the EDA uncovered

01South Australia: 24.69% of intervals below zero; Victoria: 20.35%.
02Victoria has the most separate negative price episodes, at 9,137.
03All five regions were negative at once in 5,693 intervals, or 1.12% of timestamps.
04South Australia leads the simplified battery simulation at A$455.61 per day.
Decision lens
Generators should examine negative price exposure. Buyers should examine price spikes. Storage operators need both price spreads and realistic operating costs.

From research questions to business decisions

Evidence to action
01 / Exposure South Australia and Victoria have the highest observed negative price frequencies.
02 / Timing Hourly and monthly comparisons show when below zero prices concentrate.
03 / Risk Price dispersion and extreme positive events show why averages are not enough.
04 / Flexibility Historical price spreads suggest opportunities worth testing with realistic battery economics.

Methods demonstrated

EDA skills
Data preparation

Five minute data consolidation, quality checks, date features and regional aggregation.

Descriptive statistics

Mean, median, minimum, maximum, frequency and standard deviation.

Exploration

Regional comparisons, seasonal patterns, hourly profiles and outlier analysis.

Advanced analysis

Episode detection, correlation, price spreads and scenario sensitivity.

Generators

Manage negative price exposure

Assess regional negative price frequency and duration, then review contracting and dispatch flexibility.

Retailers and consumers

Plan around price risk

Stress test extreme positive prices and investigate flexible demand where contracts allow.

Storage investors

Validate the economics

Use the historical ranking as an initial screen, then model real dispatch, fees, degradation and capital costs.

Research limitations

The analysis is descriptive, not causal. It does not include generation mix, demand, congestion or fuel costs. The 2026 data ends in October. The battery model assumes perfect foresight and omits many real costs. Historical results cannot guarantee future returns. Some earlier timestamp based intermediate files contained 2021 boundary dates and should be revalidated before publication.

Data and methodology

Source: AEMO derived regional reference prices via Australian Electricity Data Directory.
Coverage: NSW / ACT, QLD, VIC, SA and TAS, January 2022 to October 2026.
Tools: R for data preparation and analysis, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the interactive presentation.
Measure: Prices are nominal AUD per MWh.
